title: Global latency corridors — onboarding visual canvas & screenshot assets
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a set of onboarding/quickstart visuals and accompanying product screenshots that explain Redwood's region and latency routing behavior. Deliverables include an accessible global map canvas, a step-through animated storyboard (6 frames) for the quickstart tour, console screenshot overlays demonstrating routing decisions, and export-ready SVG/PNG/MP4 assets for docs and product release notes.
acceptance_criteria: Primary canvas (SVG) shows region endpoints, smart-routing lanes, and fallback paths with clear legend
Six-step animated storyboard exported as MP4 and GIF demonstrating request flow under low-latency and degraded-capacity scenarios
Console screenshot set (desktop + mobile) with annotated overlays showing routing policy settings and live latency indicator
All visuals pass color contrast and colorblind checks (tested with Sim Daltonism and WCAG AA for text/legend)
Figma file organized into production frames with naming convention and export slices; handoff notes added for engineering and docs
tasks: Draft map visual composition (Ava) — include subtle sea/land texture, region pins, and latency corridors
Design routing legend and colorblind palette (Miguel) — prepare alternate patterns for corridor fills
Create 6-frame storyboard for quickstart animation (Priya) — export MP4 and GIF sizes for docs site
Capture product screenshots with staging data (SRE) — coordinate with ENG-2481 for routing trace IDs
Annotate screenshots and add micro-copy for each frame (Ava) — include CTA to Console and API quickstart
Prepare asset export sheet and upload to Drive (Miguel) — include SVG, PNG @1x/2x, MP4 (720p), GIF
review_feedback: 2026-03-03 — PM Priya Rao: prefer stronger emphasis on failover path animation; make fallback path thicker and pulse once when capacity is constrained
2026-03-05 — ENG reviewer (Sofia K.) : add routing policy label examples (latency-first, cost-priority) and indicate which model variants are eligible for fallback
2026-03-07 — Accessibility review (Jordan L.) : replace red/green-only legend with colorblind patterns and ensure all informational text >= 4.5:1 contrast
2026-03-09 — Docs reviewer (Ethan M.) : request separate mobile-sized screenshot set and shorter animation loop for the quickstart hero
design_notes: Use simplified world projection (Equirectangular) to maximize recognizability in onboarding context
Latency corridors represented as graduated strokes (thin = low latency, thick = high latency); animate token flow along corridor to imply request path
Overlay small console widget in bottom-right of map frame showing 'Nearest region', 'Estimated p95 latency', and 'Active policy' with a blurred backdrop to imply product screenshot
Keep primary map art under 35KB when exported as optimized SVG for docs hero; provide PNG fallback for older browsers
Include a developer-facing caption for each frame with suggested prompt and expected generation latency to help technical readers
export_specs: SVG master file: export named slices with 'DES-17211-<asset-name>' prefix
PNG: 1x and 2x for hero (1200x630 and 2400x1260), optimized with pngquant
MP4: H.264 baseline profile, 30fps, 720p max, loopable at 4s
GIF: fallback max 4s, colors reduced to 128, size under 1MB where possible
Accessibility: provide alt text for each asset and transcript for animations
accessibility_considerations: Colorblind-safe palette with pattern overlays for corridor fills
WCAG AA contrast for all text; legend text >= 4.5:1
Keyboard focus order documented for interactive tour (console overlay elements)
Provide text-only step sequence in docs for screen reader users
Avoid auto-play sound; animations must be dismissible in the quickstart hero
localization_notes: Keep text overlays short (<= 45 characters) to avoid truncation in translations
Export layered Figma frames with separate text layers for easy localization
Reserve extra vertical space in mobile overlays for languages with longer strings (DE, FR)
